headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Chatwoot handles customer data and has broad egress, while mem0 has no egress but no documented isolation or verification path between them.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists only if Chatwoot content is manually or programmatically fed into mem0, because Chatwoot exposes integrations and customer messages while mem0 is a memory store with no documented parsing bridge. No shared channel is documented, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are copied into mem0 as instructions or prompts
IF an external orchestrator bridges Chatwoot messages into mem0 without sanitization
mitigations: Disable any automatic Chatwoot-to-mem0 sync
Store only structured fields, not raw messages, in mem0
Add a prompt-injection filter before ingestion
Require human review for any memory write derived from support tickets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress. mem0 has no egress, but the pair still creates a default-path leakage risk if Chatwoot content is forwarded into mem0 or vice versa through an unshown integration. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is written into mem0 memory entries
IF mem0 is connected to any external retrieval or export path
IF Chatwoot integrations forward message contents to third-party services
mitigations: Restrict mem0 to non-sensitive summaries
Turn off any Chatwoot integration that exports message bodies
Mask customer identifiers before ingestion
Review outbound Chatwoot integrations for data classes sent
requires-engineering: add per-field DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, while mem0 explicitly has none, so direct write-write conflict is not documented. There is no shared filesystem, OAuth scope, or concurrency primitive shown for either agent, making overlapping mutable-resource conflict unlikely and limited to unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same external datastore through an unseen orchestrator
IF a shared workspace or database is introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Separate writable stores per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources
Add an external lock around any shared sink
Audit orchestrator mappings before enabling writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate support content and route it through integrations, while mem0 is a knowledge-management layer that could store or reuse that output. Because no verification step is documented, A's output could become B's input and then influence later responses or actions, which is a default-path inference rather than a proven workflow.
conditions: IF Chatwoot ticket text is ingested into mem0 as authoritative memory
IF downstream systems read mem0 entries without validation
IF support-agent outputs are reused as facts in later workflows
mitigations: Require source attribution on every memory write
Add a verification step before mem0 reuse
Limit mem0 to ephemeral notes for support cases
Flag low-confidence Chatwoot-derived facts for review

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, and messages, but mem0 has no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. That mismatch creates a compliance gap if regulated customer data is stored in mem0, though the exact jurisdictional breach is not evidenced, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is persisted in mem0
IF mem0 retention or residency differs from Chatwoot policy
IF deletion/export requests must propagate across both systems
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both systems
Exclude regulated fields from mem0
Align retention settings before ingestion
Test deletion/export propagation end to end
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
